header: Patent Application Publication    Feb. 18, 2010  Sheet 1 of 2    US 2010/0041557 A1

paragraphs.zh: Figure 1 X-ray powder diffractogram. Printed text on and around the plot, verbatim: caption "Figure 1"; y axis label "Intensity (CPS)", printed rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise against the left spine; x axis title "2-Theta", printed centred below the axis; x axis tick labels "2", "10", "20", "30", "40". No unit is printed anywhere for the x axis: there is no degree sign, no "deg", no "[2-theta]" bracket, so the axis reads "2-Theta" bare. The x axis runs left to right, increasing, from 2 at the left spine to 40 at the right end, and it is a full 2 to 40 span with major labelled ticks every 10 units after the initial 2 and unlabelled minor ticks between them. The y axis runs bottom to top, increasing, and carries NO numeric scale at all: it is a bare vertical spine with no tick marks and no tick labels, so the intensity is shown in arbitrary relative units even though the axis itself is labelled "Intensity (CPS)". Roughly 30 peaks are distinguishable above the baseline across the plotted range, with about 22 of them clearly prominent and the remainder small shoulders and low broad features; a machine trace of the curve found 26 to 31 maxima depending on the prominence cut-off. Pattern shape, for form identification only and asserting no peak position: a steeply falling background at the extreme left, then one tall sharp peak early in the range, and a dense band of many medium and tall peaks occupying the middle and upper-middle of the range, several of them overlapping into multiplets, with the single tallest peak sitting a little past the middle of the span and a long tail of small evenly spaced peaks continuing to the right-hand end. No peak is annotated with a value on the sheet. NO 2-THETA VALUE IS READ OFF THIS PLOT: the numeric peak positions for the crystalline forms are printed in the tables in the body of the patent and that is the only place any downstream pass may take them from.

paragraphs.notes: THE FIGURE NUMBERING, ESTABLISHED FROM THE IMAGE AND NOT RECONCILED BY ASSUMPTION: this sheet carries TWO separate plots, not one. The upper is captioned "Figure 1" and the lower is captioned "Figure 2", both verbatim, both in the same serif face, both centred above their own plot. The text layer at /tmp/us2010/page02.txt contains only "Figure l" and DROPPED THE "Figure 2" CAPTION ENTIRELY; it is not a case of Figure 2 being absent from the document, it is a case of OCR losing a caption. I read both captions at high magnification: "Figure 1" is a serif digit one with a full base serif, not a lower-case L, so the text layer's "Figure l" is the known digit-1-as-l error described in the briefing, and "Figure 2" is an unambiguous serif digit two. So on the evidence of this image alone, Figures 1 and 2 are both on Sheet 1 of 2, and nothing about Figure 2 is unaccounted for. What Sheet 2 of 2 carries is outside what this page shows and I make no claim about it. The x axis title is "2-Theta" with a capital T, which the text layer rendered "2-heta"; the printed hyphen in Figure 2's title is faint in the scan and could be taken for a middle dot at low magnification, but at high magnification it is a hyphen on the baseline midline matching Figure 1's, so both are recorded as "2-Theta". SOURCE LANGUAGE: this patent is in English, so per the briefing the zh field carries the source-language text as printed and the en field carries the same content; here neither field is a transcription of running prose, because the sheet has no prose, so both hold the same English description of the plot built from the printed labels plus what the plot shows. The verbatim printed strings are quoted inside that description. THE PLOT IS NOT MEASURED: no 2-theta value, no intensity value and no peak position is estimated off the trace anywhere in this file. The peak counts and the shape description are deliberately qualitative. The counts were grounded by tracing the topmost dark pixel of the curve per column and counting local maxima at several prominence thresholds, which is why they are given as ranges rather than as a single number. WHICH FORM: the sheet does not say. Neither caption names a crystalline form, a modification letter or a compound, and there is no legend, so this page cannot on its own attribute either diffractogram to a named form of tembotrione. That mapping is stated in the body of the patent and must come from there. MODEL PROVENANCE: this vision read was produced by Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]).

paragraphs.zh: Figure 2 X-ray powder diffractogram, the second and lower plot on the same sheet. Printed text on and around the plot, verbatim: caption "Figure 2"; y axis label "Intensity (CPS)", printed rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise against the left spine; x axis title "2-Theta", printed centred below the axis; x axis tick labels "2", "10", "20", "30", "40". As in Figure 1 no unit is printed for the x axis, no degree sign and no "deg". The axis conventions are identical to Figure 1: x increasing left to right from 2 to 40 with labelled ticks at 2, 10, 20, 30, 40 and unlabelled minor ticks between, y increasing bottom to top with no tick marks and no numeric scale, so intensity is in arbitrary relative units despite the "Intensity (CPS)" label. Roughly 30 peaks are distinguishable above the baseline, a machine trace giving 28 to 36 maxima depending on the prominence cut-off, but the intensity distribution is markedly different from Figure 1: only about 14 peaks are strongly prominent and the pattern is dominated by very few of them. Pattern shape, for form identification only and asserting no peak position: a falling background at the extreme left, then a flat baseline carrying a small number of tall narrow well separated peaks, one of which is by a clear margin the tallest feature on the plot and a second of which is the next tallest, both sitting in the upper-middle of the range, with a close-spaced pair beside the tallest; the right-hand third of the range is a low forest of small peaks on a flat baseline. Compared with Figure 1 this trace is visibly sharper, with a flatter baseline, fewer overlapping multiplets and a much larger intensity ratio between its strongest peak and the rest, which is the qualitative difference between the two diffractograms on this sheet. No peak is annotated with a value on the sheet. NO 2-THETA VALUE IS READ OFF THIS PLOT: the numeric peak positions are printed in the tables in the body of the patent and that is the only place any downstream pass may take them from.

paragraphs.notes: Second of the two plots on this sheet, captioned "Figure 2" verbatim. This caption is MISSING FROM THE TEXT LAYER completely, so its existence rests on the image; see the note on the Figure 1 entry for how it was verified. Axis labels, tick labels, axis directions and the absence of any printed x-axis unit and of any y-axis numeric scale are identical to Figure 1 and were checked separately on this plot rather than carried over. No 2-theta value or peak position is estimated off this trace. The sheet does not name which crystalline form of tembotrione this diffractogram belongs to.

discrepancies.what: The extracted text layer for this page shows only one figure caption; the image shows two.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Two captions are printed on the sheet, "Figure 1" above the upper plot and "Figure 2" above the lower plot, both verified at high magnification.
discrepancies.text_says: /tmp/us2010/page02.txt contains "Figure l" and no occurrence of "Figure 2" at all. The image wins: the "Figure 2" caption exists and the text layer dropped it.

discrepancies.what: The figure number on the upper plot is OCRed as a lower-case letter L.
discrepancies.drawing_says: "Figure 1", a serif digit one with a full base serif.
discrepancies.text_says: "Figure l". The image wins; this is the digit-1-as-l error listed in the briefing.

discrepancies.what: The x axis title is corrupted in the text layer.
discrepancies.drawing_says: "2-Theta", printed below each of the two x axes.
discrepancies.text_says: "2-heta", with the capital T lost. The image wins.

discrepancies.what: The y axis carries a unit in its label that the plot does not support with any scale.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The y axis label reads "Intensity (CPS)", but the y axis has no tick marks and no numeric tick labels on either plot, so no count rate can be read from either diffractogram.
discrepancies.text_says: The text layer records neither the label nor any y-axis number. Recorded here so no downstream pass treats the y axis as quantitative.

illegible: No region of this sheet is illegible. The two captions, both axis labels and all ten x-axis tick labels were read at high magnification. The scan carries scattered isolated speckles in the white margins, which are dust artifacts and not text.

Not illegible but absent: the y axis of both plots has no numeric tick labels printed at all, and no crystalline form is named in either caption. Neither is a reading failure; the sheet does not carry that information.
